newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwaiti firm plans to form first investment bank.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti firm plans to form first investment bank.

text.p: State-owned Kuwait Investment Company (KIC) plans to set up the country's first investment bank, a newspaper reported on Monday.

"The benefits of the (KIC's) merger with the Kuwait Foreign Trade, Contracting and Investment Company (KFTCIC) are not only cost cutting ...it will be turned into the first Kuwaiti investment bank," al-Watan newspaper quoted KIC's chairman Bader al-Bader as saying.
Bader said the move requires the approval of the Central Bank but did not give any further details of the size or operations of the proposed investment bank.
Kuwait has six commercial banks, two specialist banks and a branch of a Bahrain-based bank.
KIC in 1994 bought the assets of state-owned KFTCIC to form a new body which retain's KIC's name. KIC will be disolved on October 8 and shareholders will swap their shares for KIC shares.
The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, in 1995 owned the majority of KIC's 50 million dinar ($166 million) capital and all of KFTCIC's 13.5 million ($49 million).

Kuwait has sought to streamline its web of state investment firms since the 1991 Gulf War to bring their operations into line with their reduced holdings of overseas assets and increase control in the wake of scandals over alleged corruption.
It has also sought to encourage reform in the banking sector, which it says suffers from excess capacity.
